text: Chalmers' 'hard problem' of consciousness is the problem of explaining:
choices: How the brain discriminates and categorizes sensory stimuli
How attention selects some information for further processing
Why there is subjective experience at all — why physical processing is accompanied by 'something it is like'
How the brain produces verbal reports about its own internal states
explanation: The hard problem asks why physical/functional processing is accompanied by phenomenal experience at all, rather than going on 'in the dark.' Options 0, 1, and 3 are precisely the easy problems — discrimination, attention, and reportability — which Chalmers grants are tractable by ordinary cognitive science. The hard problem is what remains once every easy problem is solved.
